text:
Aisha: quick weekly health check for Helio Labs 
Aisha: short TL;DR: WoW tokens down ~12%, QoQ still positive; midday p50 spike; 5xxs ticked up; spend slightly higher. Flagging ops + enablement.

Aisha: numbers snapshot:
```
metric | last_week | this_week | change
tokens | 480k | 423k | -11.8%
p50_ms | 120 | 210 | +75%
5xx_rate | 0.12% | 0.90% | +0.78pp
spend | $18.2k | $19.8k | +8.8%
```

Aisha: latency concentrated 10:00-13:00 PST yesterday; batch sizes up, KV hit-rate fell. @Miguel can you dig into logs? @Jian should we mark renewal watch?

Miguel: jumping in. pulling per-request logs and batch windows. early signal = a handful of long-sequence requests; scheduling a 30m sync at 10:30 PT to review.

Nate: quick data note: ~67% of this week's tokens from 3 client keys; one client shifted to >1024 token seqs the day of the spike. I uploaded a small CSV to the secure gist (placeholder link).

Miguel: hypothesis: workload shift -> more KV misses -> larger processing time -> p50 jump. I like to check model-variant fallbacks and node-level evictions in the same window.

Priya: suggested enablement: 20-min session for Helio devs on prompt windowing and truncation plus quick guide on batching best-practices. I can prepare materials for next Tue.

Jian: renewal view: account-health score moved 74 -> 62 this check. Marking as "watch". Recommend auto-escalate if next check <=60. Not urgent yet but monitor.

deploy-bot: Anomaly AD-4421: correlated model-variant fallback events and increased latency detected 2024-09-12T10:05Z - 2024-09-12T12:55Z.

Miguel: confirmed fallback flags in selector logs; possible capacity-induced fallback to a slower quantized variant. Will verify node capacity and evictions.

Aisha: agreed action items:
- Miguel + Nate: deep-dive + raw CSV + short findings by EOD today.
- Priya: schedule enablement (20m + one-pager) for next Tue.
- Jian: set renewal-risk = watch; CS owner to escalate if health <=60 next check.

Miguel: will post query results and per-client batch windows.

Nate: will attach prefix-cache hit-rate chart to the CSV.

Aisha: thanks all ":thumbsup:", I post a short summary in #customer-success tomorrow morning.
